text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a spike in error+latency today around 09:12 UTC. Root cause looks like routing to unavailable AMD kernels for a small set of op casings (mixed seq lengths ~128-1024). Fallback to CPU happened and P50 jumped ~3x.
kevin: Ugh. Any repro logs or request ids?
maria: Pasted a short trace from the router logs (trimmed):
```
[09:12:03] route_decision id=svc-123 path=amd:fp16:opset-7 missing_kernel=matmul_128x256 -> fallback=cpu
[09:12:03] runtime_exec id=svc-123 backend=cpu latency=245ms seq_len=512
[09:12:04] trace id=svc-124 route=amd:fp16 selected_kernel=matmul_64x128 success
```
kevin: Looks like kernel availability is conditional on op shapes + build matrix. Might be a packaging hole for matmul_128x256 on our AMD build.
zach: We saw a similar hole last month but for attention kernels. Two thoughts: 1) router should avoid hard routing to a kernel that isn't present on the node; 2) add a soft-fallback policy that tries nearest-compatible AMD kernel before CPU.
dalia: Agreed. Right now the routing code chooses kernel by exact signature then falls back to (node-level) next-tier. It doesn't probe for compatible variants.
maria: Impact notes: ~0.8% of requests in the window hit the fallback path, but they were 90th-percentile user-facing queries (longer seqs). Customer reported latency regressions.
rui: Can we get perf-bot to run a quick profile of the node group that served those requests? Need timeline + loaded kernels list.
perf-bot: Scheduled perf snapshot: group=amd-prod-02 start=09:10 end=09:20. Uploading flamegraphs to /opt/perf/reports/1777777777.
sam: From the flamegraph, the CPU fallback dominated token time for the affected traces. Also noticed KV cache miss amplification when fallback happened — because fallback path uses a different KV-key prefix, cache hit rate dropped.
kevin: KV cache prefix change explains bursty upstream work. Two fixes: keep a stable KV prefix across kernel variants or ensure fallback reuses same prefix (preferable).
zach: For kernel routing heuristics, propose these immediate actions:
- router: pre-check node kernel table before committing route (cheap set lookup)
- router: add 'closest-compat' policy to select kernel with compatible shape/quantization instead of falling to CPU
- autotuner: feed it seq-length histogram so it prefers short-seq kernels for 0-64 and different ones for 256+

dalia: Implementation notes: pre-check adds ~0.5ms to route decision if we query remote; do local cache of node kernel manifests with TTL 10s to keep latency low. Also include a probe path: when a route fails with missing kernel, emit a "missing_kernel" metric with shape signature.
maria: +1. Also let's add a canary rollout for 'closest-compat' to 5% of traffic. We need metrics: fallback-rate, cpu-fallback-latency, kv-hit-rate-by-route.
kevin: I'll add telemetry tags and a dashboard. Can we mitigate immediately by backfilling the missing matmul_128x256 artifact into the AMD package?
rui: We can push a hotfix build to one AZ tonight. But longer term we want router resilience — not just packaging fixes.
sam: Small note on autotuner data: the current tuner aggregates by model+device but not by sequence-length bucket. I'll add seq_len buckets [0-64,65-256,257-1024,1025+]. That should reduce mis-picks.
perf-bot: Quick stats from snapshot: cpu-fallback_count=42, avg_cpu_fallback_latency=210ms, avg_amd_success_latency=45ms, kv_hit_rate_pre=0.78 post_fallback_window=0.41.
kevin: Oof. That kv hit drop is the scary part.
zach: Action items:
- kevin: dashboard + alerts for cpu-fallback-rate and kv-hit-drop (ETA 24h)
- rui: schedule hotfix package to one AZ (ETA tonight)
- sam: change autotuner to include seq_len buckets and start training next cycle (ETA 3d)
- maria/dalia: implement router pre-check + closest-compat policy & TTL cache (ETA 5d), canary at 5%
- perf-bot: add trace link to dashboard for quick triage (ETA 48h)

maria: Also logging hygiene: when fallback occurs we should attach the chosen fallback kernel id and the attempted kernel signature so we can debug quickly.
kevin: Good call. Add structured fields: attempted_kernel, fallback_kernel, node_kernel_manifest_version.
maria: Cool — thanks all. I'll create the RFC for router change and assign tasks. For now, monitor the hotfix AZ and I'll post updates in this thread. :thumbsup: 
infra-bot: Deploy trigger accepted for hotfix build to az-3 (job=hotfix-amd-matmul-128x256). CI: green.
maria: Update 11:45 UTC — hotfix deployed to az-3, initial metrics show cpu-fallback_count down to 3 in that AZ, kv-hit-rate recovered to 0.76. Continuing rollout after verification window.
kevin: Great. Let's iterate router changes after we validate canary.
